Hola, cariño! Have you eaten today? Look — El Tatuador, five P for you, a good card to start with. And here, take La Chulapa too, a little present, because you asked so nicely. No, no, keep it, hijo.

Oh, oh... 6 P, and only because you have a kind face. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Oh, oh... 25 P, and only because you have a kind face.
One point from you, one from me. Fourteen. Las Vistillas. That is the number now.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment, have you eaten? Look here — La Corrala, one of my favourites. A boy traded me this one twenty years ago, now he brings his own children. For you, five P. Take your time looking, hijo, no hurry.

Ay, hijo, you bargain like my nephew Paquito! But 5 P is my offer, and it is a good one. Take it and buy yourself a bocadillo, you look hungry. And listen, cariño — a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, qué simpático eres, hijo. Siete está un poquito flojo para mi Paseo de Coches… mira, diez P y nos damos la mano como buenos vecinos. Mi marido decía que los tratos buenos se cierran con una sonrisa. ¿Y tú, ya has comido algo hoy, cariño?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Two more. Bueno. Thirteen. Same as before, same as next time. Straight deal or go walk the Rastro.

Ay, hijo, you ask so sweetly, but this is my last word: the Escaparate de Serrano, 6 P. If no, I fold the table and we stay friends anyway. Have you eaten? And go see El Chato at half past nine, cariño.
Ay, hijo, you stretch like my old cardigan! Look, 24 P, and I wrap it nice so it does not bend in your bag. Eat something after, cariño, you look thin.

Ay, qué simpático eres, hijo! But eleven... no, no, that one makes my table cry. Look, 25 P, and I am being soft like bread. Keep your duplicates for El Chato tonight, half past nine — he is fair with people who trade straight. ¿Has comido ya?

Ay, hijo, ten? No, no — five P is what I said, and five P it stays. I am not here to empty your pockets. Keep the rest for a bocadillo. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Look, 24 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Oh, oh... 23 P, and only because you have a kind face.

Ay, cariño, you are stubborn like my nephew! Nine, no. Five P, that is my price and I am happy with it. Put the rest in your pocket for churros. La Corrala goes home with you tonight — and remember, swap those duplicates, hijo!

¡Ay, cariño, qué amable! Siéntate, que no hay prisa. Mira, yo te digo mi oferta: el Té Moruno por 5 P. Es bonita para empezar, hijo. ¿Has comido ya? Siempre digo lo mismo, pero una barriga vacía no regatea bien.

Ay, está bien, cariño — 6 P, and we shake on it! You wear me down like my Paquito. Now go eat something, hijo. And listen, Doña Pilar from Salamanca comes Saturday at eleven — she pays very well for her favourites. Bring her your duplicates!
You again. Guantería Antigua. Thirty-three. That's the number.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Thirty-three. Same number as a minute ago. It does not move because you smiled.

¡Ay, qué educado eres, hijo! Look, 22 P for the Fuente de la Alcachofa, and I put in a little present — "Puesto del Rastro," my own stall, see? Because you ask so nicely. Now promise me you eat something, cariño, you look thin.

Ay, qué cabezota eres, hijo! Eight, no. Five P, like I told you — La Corrala for five P and that is that. Take the card, take your coins, go eat something hot. And swap those duplicates, cariño, your page will thank you!
Two at a time, eh? Patience is cheap today. Thirteen. It was thirteen an hour ago. Keep walking down; I'll be here, not moving.

Buenos días, hijo! Have you eaten? Come, sit a moment. Let me show you something bonito — the Escaparate de Serrano, I can let it go for 5 P. Forty years I sit at this table, and that one still makes me smile.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Have you eaten? Such a pretty card, yes, and your album sounds lovely. But my little table is humble, hijo. I can give you five for it. That is my offer — five, and a smile from the abuela.

Ay, cariño, fifteen! You make my old heart laugh. Look, 23 P, and I am giving you my best smile with it. Eat something, hijo, you look thin. And remember El Chato tonight, half past nine — swap your duplicates, he is fair.
Look, 22 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Look, 21 P. My grandchildren would pay more! Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Thirty-three. You moved one. That buys you nothing here. Come back when your number is serious.

Ay, hijo, twenty is a dream for an abuela like me. But listen — my Café de Madrugada, a pretty one, I give you that for five. Think of it, cariño, no prisa. Have a little something to eat first, and then you tell me.

Ay, qué labia tienes, hijo. Pero mi oferta sigue siendo la misma: Té Moruno por 5 P. No te enfades conmigo, ¿eh? Y escucha: El Chato, aquí al lado, abre a las nueve y media esta noche. Le gusta la gente que trata derecho.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a little, you look hungry — have you eaten? Look here, this one is La Corrala, very pretty, the kids always want her. For you, twelve P. My grandson traded me three duplicates for his, poor angel.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.

Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 10 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Thirty-two. You moved one, I moved one. That's how it works. Your turn.

Ay, cariño, you are sweet, but my old purse is slow. Five P is what I can say, the same as before — 5 P for the Escaparate de Serrano. Sit, have a mandarina. Take your time, hijo, nobody is rushing here.

Ay, cariño, nineteen is too many for this old table. But my Café de Madrugada for five — it is pretty, it would look lovely on your page. And El Chato, next to me, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight; he likes straight traders like you.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, you look hungry — have you eaten? Look here, this one is La Galería, a beautiful complete page, all the cards together. For you, 29 P. My grandson started with this very one, many years ago.

Ay, your abuela too? Then she would scold me, hijo. The neighbourhood pack, 21 P — and that is my last word, cariño. If no, I pack up and we stay friends anyway. Go eat something. And El Chato tonight, half past nine, trade straight.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Thirty-two. You moved one, I already moved mine. Last number I say tonight. Take it or walk.
Buenas. La Fiesta de San Cayetano: 97. Ese es mi número, no el tuyo.
Buenas. Book value is a story people tell. Here, that card goes for 33 P.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Palacio de Velázquez — very pretty, no? For you, 29 P.

And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!
Ay, qué amable, hijo. Twenty-two is a little thin for a whole page, mira — all of them together like a family. Let us say 26 P and I sleep happy. Take a caramelo from the tin too, you look hungry.

Ay, hijo, four? For La Corrala? She is the prettiest on the table, mira. No, no — I stay at 10 P, that is already my friend price. Eat something first, then come back. And remember El Chato, half past nine — he likes honest traders like you.

¡Trato hecho, cariño! Seis primas y el Té Moruno es tuyo. Mira qué bien has negociado, hijo, con paciencia y buenas palabras. Anda, guárdalo bien y come algo, que estás muy flaco. Y no olvides a El Chato esta noche, a las nueve y media. ¡Vuelve a verme!

Ay, hijo, eighteen my old purse never saw. But look — my Café de Madrugada, I give it to you for six. Pretty, no? It would shine on your page. No prisa, cariño, think a little. And remember El Chato, half past nine tonight.
Oh, oh... 9 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 26 P.
You move, I move. 97 P.
You moved four. I moved nothing. Still 33 P. House market takes five per cent, by the way. Other stalls charge less. Look around if you like.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? This one here, the Neighbourhood pack, thirty P — good cards for starting out. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates with friends.

Ay, cariño, sixteen my little purse has never held, de verdad. But my Café de Madrugada — six, and it is yours. A little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. No prisa, think a little.

Ay hijo, you bargain with a smile, like my nietos. But 5 P is my last word — if that does not suit you, we part as friends, no hard feelings. And listen: Doña Pilar from Salamanca comes Saturday at eleven, she pays very well. Eat something, cariño.

Ay, está bien, hijo — 24 P, and it is yours. Vale, the page stays whole, that is what matters to me. Here, take two caramelos, you still look hungry. My grandson will be happy somebody else starts with La Galería. ¡Que lo disfrutes, cariño!
Look, 25 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Subiste cuatro, bajo dos. 95 P. Así funciona conmigo.

Ay, hijo, seven... you squeeze this old woman like a lemon! No, 9 P, that is where I stay — she is worth it, you'll see. Have you eaten something? Go, and come back at half past nine for El Chato; he likes straight traders like you.

Ay, hijo, you bargain like my grandson! Look — 25 P, and I wrap it nice for you. This card has waited years for someone who smiles like that. And eat something after, ¿eh? The churro man is just by the corner.

Ay, hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one, La Galería — such a pretty card, my favorite since many years. For you, twelve P. My grandson started his album with one just like it.

Ay, hijo, fifteen is not for this old table, de verdad. My Café de Madrugada, six, and it is yours — pretty, it would shine on your page. But cariño, this is my last offer. If no, we say adiós with a kiss, sin rencor.
Oh, oh... 24 P, and only because you have a kind face.
No. 93 P, and I'm being generous.

You moved four. I still have not moved. Thirty-three. That is what is keeping us apart, amigo.

Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Subiste cuatro, bajo cuatro. 89 P. Yo cuento igual que tú.
Twenty-one? For that I'd throw in my chair. Thirteen. Same as a minute ago. Take it or walk, amigo.

Ay, you flatter an old woman, cariño! Twenty-two P, and not because of the pretty words — because your abuela would want you to start right. Take it, eat something, and go see El Chato at half past nine. He likes honest traders like you.

Ay, cariño, you are too generous with this old woman. Fifteen P, and not one more — my conscience would not let me sleep. Take her home, she likes company. And eat something, hijo, you look thin. Sunday you come tell me how your album grows, ¿vale?

¡Ay, cariño! You push and push, like my own nietos. 24 P — that is my last word, hijo. If it does not suit you, we leave it, no hard feelings, and you go eat something warm. But I wrap it beautiful for 24 P.
You move, I move. 85 P.

Oh, oh... 21 P, and only because you have a kind face. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
One point. That's your "coming down"? Thirteen. Still thirteen. I don't move first, chaval.

Ay, hijo, you are stubborn like my nephew! But five P is my word, and a fair one. Perrito con Abrigo, five P, and the bicycle still goes with you, gratis. Keep your duplicates, swap them at El Chato — fill your page, cariño. Have you eaten today?

Ay, no, hijo, nineteen — you want me to feel like a thief! Fifteen P, that is my price and I will not move. La Galería goes with you tonight. Now go eat something warm, and Sunday you come tell me everything, ¿vale, cariño?

¡Buenos días, cariño! ¿Has desayunado algo? El Titiritero es bonito, sí, como los títeres del barrio. Te lo dejo en 12. Y un consejo, hijo: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas, así que cambia tus repetidas. Vuelve el domingo y me enseñas el álbum.
Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
Look, 12 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Nineteen. You're crawling. Thirteen. I said it three times, I'll say it a fourth. Move properly or don't move.
84. Hecho. Fiesta de San Cayetano es tuya. Dealt straight, I remember that.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look, this one — Barca del Estanque, very pretty, yes? For you, twelve P.

And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always.

Ay, cariño, you push and push — but with such good manners! Bueno, sixteen P, and that is because you make an old woman laugh. La Galería goes with you tonight. Now eat something warm, hijo, and Sunday you tell me how your album grows, ¿vale?

¡Hola, hijo! ¿Has comido ya? Qué carta más bonita, sí señor. Pero mira, yo te doy cinco primas por ella, que es lo justo para esta vieja. Si quieres cosas mejores, El Chato, el puesto de al lado, abre para todos a las nueve y media esta noche.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 10 P.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Flattery's free. Eighteen isn't partway, it's a shuffle. Thirteen. Fifth time. Say something real or take your card home.
Zero fee is your gift to yourself, not to me. Card is thirty-three. Your stall, my stall, same number.

Ay, bueno, seventeen P — you win, cariño, and my heart is glad. Take her, she likes company. Trato hecho! Now go eat something warm, hijo, you look thin. And Sunday you come back and tell this old woman how your album grows, ¿vale?

Ay, hijo, qué bien hablas. Mira, lo dejamos en 10 y todos contentos, ¿eh? El Titiritero se va a una buena casa. Pero cómete algo antes, que estás flaquito. Y el domingo me traes el álbum, que quiero verlo con mis ojos.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? This one here, the Neighbourhood pack, is 30 P — good cards for starting, I promise. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates with the other niños!
Oh, oh... 25 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You again. La Rosaleda. Thirty-three. Good card, fair price. Decide quick, I have other customers.

Ay, cariño, qué insistente eres, me recuerdas a mi nieto. Pero mi bolsillo es pequeño: cinco primas por la Mercado de la Cebada, ni una más. Y un consejo, hijo: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas! ¿Seguro que has comido?

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — this Té Moruno, a pretty one, I let it go for 5 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!

Ay, hijo, you bargain like my grandson — he never ate breakfast either! But ten P is my number, and a fair one. Take the Barca, finish your page, and come back Sunday with your duplicates. I keep good things for good people, cariño.

Buenos días, cariño! Qué guapo, coming so early. Have you eaten? Look, this one here, Perrito con Abrigo, a little dog in a coat, very sweet. Five P and he is yours. My first customer today, so I feel generous.
Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look here — La Corrala, one of my favourites, a boy traded me this one twenty years ago. For you, twelve P. A good card to begin with, hijo.
Look, 9 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.

Ay, hijo, you make me laugh! Ten? No, no — for you the Té Moruno is 5 P, the same as always. Take it, put it in your album, and come back Sunday with your duplicates. Have you eaten something today? Go on, cariño.
Ay, cariño, eleven! Look — 24 P, and I put in a little story for free. Tell your friends, yes, but tell them Carmen fed them too. Have you eaten anything today, hijo?

Ay, hijo, qué cabezón eres, igual que mi Antonio. Pero no cambio: cinco primas por la Mercado de la Cebada, y te las doy con cariño. Si quieres más, El Chato abre a las nueve y media, le gusta la gente que trata derecho. Anda, come algo.

Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Buenas. Cine Doré, 97. Ese es el precio que vale.
The mayor. Claro. Twenty years here, never needed him. Keep your friends, amigo. Card is thirty-three.

Ay hijo, thirteen... you have a good heart but a thin purse! Look — 23 P, and that is Carmen being soft again. Take it, go eat something, and tonight see El Chato for your duplicates. He likes boys who trade straight, like you.

Ay, hijo, you are a sweet one, but five P is my price and my heart is set. Perrito con Abrigo deserves a good home, and five P buys him for you today. Take him, cariño, and go eat something warm before the stalls close.

Ay, hijo, four? My knees are older than that card! Ten P it stays, and that is me being soft already. Take it, swap your duplicates — a full page is worth much more than loose cards. And eat something, you look thin, cariño.

Ay, cariño, you are stubborn like my nephew Julián! But no — the Té Moruno is 5 P, same as always, same as for everybody. Take it, put it in the album, and bring me your duplicates next Sunday. And eat something, hijo, you look thin.

Ay, cariño, you push like my Tomás! Nine P, and I wrap it nice for you. That card finishes your page, you know — the rest will look sad without her. Nine P, and next Sunday bring your duplicates. And eat something, hijo!

Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
No. 96 P, and I'm being generous.

Ay, hijo, qué cabezón! Look, you wear me down like my Julián — six, then, six P for the Té Moruno, and not a céntimo more talking. Take it, put it in your album, and bring me duplicates on Sunday. Now go eat something, cariño, please.
Tres pasos tuyos, tres míos. 95 P. Ese es el número.

Ay, cariño, five? You bargain like my late husband, que en paz descanse. Ten P, and that is my word — La Corrala goes home with you today. Swap your duplicates too, a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Now go eat something, hijo.

Ay, hijo, you say the same number like a little parrot! Nine P, and I wrap her in paper so she arrives pretty. My Tomás pushed like this too, and still he eats at my table on Sundays. Nine P, cariño — and bring your duplicates.

Ay, cariño, no, no — six is six, and six it stays. I already moved for you once, like a tonta. Six P, the Té Moruno is yours, pretty as anything. Put it in your album, bring me duplicates Sunday... and go eat something, hijo, por favor.

Ay, cariño, six, five... my old head only holds one number, and it is five P. Doña Pilar from Salamanca comes Saturday at eleven, she pays well for her favourites, but today the perrito is yours for five. Now go, eat something warm.

Oh, oh... 9 P, and only because you have a kind face. Eh, eh. Be nice to your abuela. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

89 P. Último. Te mueves tú, me muevo yo — ya no más. Si no, recojo y cada uno a su casa.

Buenas. La Rosaleda, 33 P. Book value is one thing; what I sell them for is another. That's my number.

Ay, hijo, seven I cannot. But look — six P, and I throw in my Vinilo de la Movida, a pretty one. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates! Six, con cariño.

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment — have you eaten? This one here, Las Vistillas, I let you have for 12 P. A pretty card, my grandson loved it too. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look, this one is La Castañera, very pretty, my favourite since many years. For you, twelve P. She starts a collection beautifully, hijo. Many children began right here at this table.

Ay, qué zalamero, cariño. Siéntate, que llevas cara de no haber comido. Mira, te doy El Frutero de Argumosa por 5 P, una carta preciosa para empezar tu álbum. Y si buscas sobres mejores, El Chato, aquí al lado, abre a las nueve y media.

Ay, cariño, you wear me down with sweetness, not with pesetas. Still five, hijo — El Frutero de Argumosa for 5. It is what these hands hold. Sit, rest. El Chato next door has the fancy packs, but he never asks if you have eaten.

Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Cash is nice. One peseta is not movement. 33 P. Still my number.

Ay, hijo, you have a good heart, and I will not forget it. But this is my last word, cariño: El Frutero de Argumosa for 5. If it is no, then no — we part friends and I stay at my table. Still, go eat something.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment — have you eaten? This one here, La Corrala, she is a beauty. Twelve P for you, hijo. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates, eh?

Ay, cariño, twenty-four! You flatter my little table. No, no — for you, thirteen P and the card goes home with you tonight. My grandson paid me nothing for his, so you see I am already soft. Eat something after, eh? Thirteen, and we are friends.
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Qué amable, pero today let me give you something. ¿Has comido ya? Look — Plaza del Dos de Mayo, a beautiful card, only 5 P for you. My grandson started his album with that very one, hijo.

Ay, hijo, qué bonito hablas, pero mi precio es el mismo que te dije: El Frutero de Argumosa, 5 P. Es carta de las buenas, me la trajo un niño hace años. Llévatela y come algo. Y El Chato abre a las nueve y media.
¡Ay, qué tozudo eres, hijo! Like my nephew Paquito, always the same face. Mira, ten P and she is yours, with a little paper bag so she does not bend. Go on, take her home and eat something, cariño.

Ay, hijo, you keep pushing the number up — such a polite boy! But no, I say thirteen P and thirteen it stays. I sleep better that way. Take it home, put it in your album, and come tell me Sunday. Have you eaten yet, cariño?
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
You again. La Rosaleda. Thirty-three. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.

Ay, cariño, you are very sweet, but my number does not move. Thirteen P, same as before, and I will not change it next Sunday either. Take Las Vistillas home, put her in your album, and go eat something warm, hijo. Thirteen, and we are friends.
Twenty-four is not market, that's hope. You move one at a time, I don't move at all. 33 P. House market takes five per cent, by the way. Look around.

Ay, hijo, four? You will make this old woman laugh until Sunday. Look — nine P, and I wrap it nice for you. La Corrala deserves a good page, not a pocket. Go see El Chato after, half past nine, he likes straight traders. Have you eaten, cariño?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 9 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look — La Rosaleda, a beautiful card, I let you have it for 29 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, hijo, qué bonita card, I see you love it. But my old purse is small today — 5 P, that is my little offer, same as before. Take it, and bring me your duplicates next Sunday. ¿Seguro que has comido? Go eat something, cariño.

Ay, hijo, you meet me partway going the wrong way! Thirteen P, same as always, and not a céntimo different. Take her, put her in your album next to the others — a full page, remember. And then go eat something warm, cariño. Thirteen, and we are friends.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Qué detalle, thank you. Sit a moment — have you eaten? Let me look at it... bonita, sí. For me, I can give you 5 for it. Is a little table, hijo, but the niños always come back for more.

Ay, cariño, you repeat like my radio in the morning. Ten P, and that is with love, not with greed. La Castañera has waited here many Sundays for someone like you. Take her, and go eat something warm, hijo — you look thin to me.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — Fuente de la Alcachofa, one of my favourites, the fountain with the little artichoke. Twenty-nine P, and she is yours. She would look lovely in your album, no?

Ay, cariño, qué ilusión me haces tú a mí. Pero ya ves, soy vieja y terca: El Frutero de Argumosa, 5 P, ni una más ni una menos. Llévatela y cómete un bocadillo, que estás flaco. Y El Chato abre a las nueve y media.
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Treinta y tres. Dije treinta y tres. El precio no se mueve porque hables rápido. Cierra o camina.

Ay, eight it is, hijo! Done. Take her, I wrap her nice for you. Put her on a full page, that is where she shines — swap your duplicates, cariño. And go see El Chato at half past nine, he likes straight traders like you. Now, have you eaten?

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look here — the Bici de Reparto, very pretty card, one of my favourites. For you, five P. It starts a nice collection, hijo. My hands have sold this table forty years, eh?
One peseta at a time. Fine. I'll match it once: 32 P. Move properly, and I'll move properly.

Ay, hijo, qué cariño tienes tú. Seventeen... no, mi vida, she has been with me a long time. Twenty-five P, and I wrap her nice for your album. You know, my nieto used to sit under that fountain eating pipas. ¿Sí?

Ay, cariño, enough dancing! Thirteen P — that is my last word. If you say no, I fold the table and we are still friends, eh? But no more offers from me. Thirteen, take Las Vistillas home, fill that page with your duplicates. Now go eat something warm, hijo.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 26 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, qué bueno, churros — eso es desayuno de verdad. Mira, hijo, 5 is what these old hands can give, still 5. But take this too, a little present: "Palacio de Velázquez." For being kind to an old woman. Keep it, cariño, it brings suerte.

¡Ay, está bien, cariño! 6 P, hecho. You have the patience of a saint, and a kind face too. Take it — and remember, a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. Doña Pilar from Salamanca pays very well, Saturdays at eleven. ¡Ahora ve a comer, hijo!

Ay, cariño, qué historias bonitas cuentas. But these old hands, they still say 5 — "Puesto del Rastro," mira, it even looks like my little table, no? Five, hijo, con mucho cariño. If you want more, El Chato next door has the fancy packs.
Buenas. Kind, me? New one. Palacio de Velázquez — thirteen primas. That is the number.
Buenas tardes, caballero. Kind, yes; foolish, never. The Palacio de Velázquez — El Retiro, my beloved Retiro — I offer you 22 primas. A fair figure, and I do not haggle like a market woman.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit, have you eaten? Look at this one, El Frutero de Argumosa — a beautiful card, very popular with the little ones. For you, twelve P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
¡Ay, hijo, my ears work fine! Ten P, same as before, same as after. I am old but not confused. La Castañera goes in the little bag, you go home and eat. Ten P, cariño, and we are friends still.
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 10 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

payload.text: 🧩 La Última Pieza: tu repetida puede completar otra página. El Duende v02: 0% + 0 P/carta. / Missing a card? Post a bid or spare-card ask with venue="v02" at your own value limits. Find the other half of your trade.

Ay, tissue paper — yes! That is how my mother kept them too, smelling of lavender. Nineteen is still too little, mi vida. Twenty-three P, and I wrap her for you in tissue, like your abuela did. ¿Trato hecho, cariño?

Ay, qué bueno, hijo — put it on your album page, it shines there. But mira, I am a simple woman with a folding table. Five for your bonita card, still five, and you keep "Puesto del Rastro." Think about it slow, cariño. No prisa.
One peseta again. I matched you once; I don't do it twice for the same crumb. 32 P. Make a real step, chaval.

Ay, buenos días, cariño! Come, sit a moment, you look hungry — have you eaten? Look here, this one is lovely: Vermut del Domingo. Twelve P for you. My grandson started his album with this very card, and now he beats his father every Sunday. Beautiful, no?

Ay, qué majo eres. Mira, hijo: 24 P and we are both happy, ¿sí? La Rosaleda will look lovely on your page. And remember — swap your duplicates with the other children, that is how my own son filled his album.
You again. La Tabacalera, thirty-three. Silver pack, good one. Take it or walk.
You. Abuela sent you, no? Fine. La Rosaleda — thirty-three. That is the number. Look all you want, it does not change.

Ay, hijo, you bargain like my grandson. Bueno — nine P, and I will not say another word about it. Take it, and remember: swap your duplicates, fill the page. And El Chato opens at half past nine tonight — he likes people who trade straight. ¿Has comido algo, cariño?

Ay, hijo, twenty-four! You are too kind, but no — I would feel like a thief. Thirteen P, and that is only because I wrapped it in paper for you. Take it, start your album, and come back Sunday to tell me how it goes.
You're Carmen's friend. La Rosaleda, 33 P.

Ay, hijo, qué paciencia tienes conmigo. But mira, this is my last word: 5 for your bonita card, and "Puesto del Rastro" stays with you, un regalo. Five, cariño — if no, we just drink café and stay friends, no hard feelings.

Ay, cariño, we have danced enough for one Sunday. Ten P was my word, and today I close my little bag. No hard feelings — come back next week and we chat again. And a tip, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates. Go eat!
Look, 9 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Another crumb. Fine, I match it: 31 P. You keep counting to one, we'll be here till Navidad. Step properly and this ends.

¡Trato hecho, cariño! 23 P y La Rosaleda es tuya. Take it, qué ilusión me hace. Now go eat something, hijo, you look thin. And swap your duplicates with the other children — that page will be full before you know it.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? This one here, Paseo de Coches, very pretty card, my favourite of the whole set. For you, twelve P. Forty years I sell here, and still this one makes me smile.
You moved one. So did I — back to 33. La Rosaleda, 33 P. Card's worth it. Your album, your choice.

Ay, qué terco eres, hijo — just like my nieto. Twenty-two P, and we stop haggling and have a little chat instead, ¿sí? And listen, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato next door always has spares.

Ay, cariño, you keep pushing the price up! You will ruin yourself. Fourteen P, and not one more — my conscience is old but it still works. Take the card, eat something warm, and tell me Sunday how your album grows, ¿vale?
Thirty-three. Same number as a minute ago. I do not move first, chaval. Thirty-three, and La Rosaleda is yours.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 10 P.
Four more from you. Nothing from me. Thirty-three, same as before. Card doesn't shrink because your budget did.

Ay, hijo, twenty-one! You will have me crying into my coffee. Fourteen P, same as before — my conscience does not move on Sundays. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. ¿Has comido ya?

¡Hecho, cariño! Eight P, and El Frutero is yours. Take it with my blessing — fill that page, swap your duplicates, and go see El Chato at half past nine. He likes people who trade straight, like you. Now go eat something, hijo. ¡Hasta el domingo!

¡Buenos días, cariño! Forty years, sí, and still the same wobbly table. Have you eaten? Listen, for a page like yours I offer you La Rosaleda — twenty-nine. A beautiful card, hijo, my favourite one. It will look lovely beside your others, you will see.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 25 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
One from you, one from me. Thirty-two. La Rosaleda. That's the give you asked for.
Sixteen. Cute. Thirty-three, same as a minute ago. Numbers don't move because you say them twice.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit, have you eaten? Look here, this one, the Bici de Reparto — a beauty, twelve P for you. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!
Ay, hijo, you push a little, I like that. Seven is too thin for my Paseo de Coches. Say nine P and I wrap it nice for your album. Then you go eat something, you look hungry to me.

Ay, cariño, you are too generous for this old table. Fourteen P — and that is my last word, truly. If you say no, I wrap it up again and we stay friends, ¿eh? No hard feelings, never. But fourteen, or nothing today. ¿Has comido algo?

Ay, diecisiete, cariño... you wear me down like the rain wears the stones. Look — 21 P, and I will not go telling El Chato how soft I am tonight. Take it, go eat something warm, and come back next Sunday with your duplicates, hijo.
Another single step. I match it, no more. 30 P for La Rosaleda. Keep crawling and we'll both grow old here, chaval.

Oh, oh... 20 P, and only because you have a kind face. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Oh, oh... 9 P, and only because you have a kind face. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 11 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
One from you, one from me. Thirty-one. La Rosaleda. That's my last word — no more steps. Take it, or I keep the card.

¡Ay, hijo, qué bien que has desayunado! Mira, bajo otra vez por ti: 23 por La Rosaleda. No puedo más, cariño, es mi favorita. Lleva tus repetidas a El Chato, él cambia bien, y así completas la página. Ya verás qué bonita queda.
You again. Palacio de Velázquez. Thirty-three P. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look, this one, Palacio de Velázquez — very pretty, no? For you, 29 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Two points from you. Fine. Thirty-two. That's my step, same size as yours. Keep walking up, I keep walking down. Slowly.

Ay, hijo, four! You make this abuela laugh. Look — ten P, and I will not move again, I promise. Have you eaten anything today? Go see El Chato tonight at half past nine, he likes honest traders. And swap those duplicates, cariño, fill your page!

¡Ay, cariño, qué chico tan dulce! Mira, 22 por La Rosaleda, y ya no me queda más que bajar, hijo. Es mi favorita, de verdad. Lleva tus repetidas a El Chato, cámbialas, y esa página tuya quedará preciosa. Una página completa vale mucho más que las sueltas.

Ay, hijo, buenos días. ¿Has comido ya? Larga sí, pero bonita. La Guantería Antigua te la dejo en 29 primas, cariño. Y un consejo: una página completa vale mucho más que las sueltas, ¡cambia tus repetidas! El Chato, el puesto de al lado, abre a las nueve y media esta noche.

Ay, cariño, you keep asking so sweetly! But nine P is my price, and nine P it stays. I wrap it in paper for your album, pretty and safe. Then you go eat a bocadillo, you look thin to me. Bring your duplicates next Sunday, eh?
Look, 9 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 10 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Buenos días. Seven. Cute. La Rosaleda, thirty-three. That is where we start.
Veintisiete. No. Treinta y tres, same as before. You moved, I did not. Card's worth it. Take it or walk.

¡Ay, hijo, qué paciencia tienes conmigo! Mira, 21 por La Rosaleda, y ya está. Es mi favorita, de verdad. El Chato abre para todos a las nueve y media esta noche — le gusta la gente que cambia de frente. Lleva tus repetidas, cariño. Esa página florecerá, ya verás.
Look, 26 P. My grandchildren would pay more!

Ay, cariño, no te pongas así, que no hay prisa. Mira, por ser tú, te la dejo en 25 primas. Mi nieto empezó igual, con poquito, y hoy tiene la página completa. Anda, ¿seguro que has desayunado algo? Tómate tu tiempo, hijo.
Nine. You moved two. I did not move. Thirty-three for La Rosaleda. Albums get built slow, chaval.
You made it past Abuela. Bien. Fuente de la Alcachofa — thirty-three. That's the number.

Ay, cariño, five! You have a good heart but a thin purse, eh? Ten P, as I said, and I keep my word. Go eat something, hijo. And swap your duplicates — a full page is worth far more than loose cards. El Chato opens at half past nine.

¡Ay, cariño, qué bonito lo dices! Mira, 20 por La Rosaleda, y ya me tiemblan las manos de bajar tanto. Es mi favorita, hijo. Ve donde El Chato con tus repetidas, cámbialas bien, y esa página tuya florecerá. ¿Seguro que has comido bien hoy?

Ay, hijo, you ask and ask with that sweet face! But the Paseo de Coches goes for nine P, no less. I wrap it in paper, pretty for your album. Then eat something, por favor. And bring your duplicates Sunday — a full page is worth much more.

Ay, cariño, qué insistente! Nine P, the same as last Sunday and the one before. I will wrap it in paper so your album stays pretty. Now, have you eaten? Go get a bocadillo, hijo — and bring your duplicates next week, we make a full page together.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 9 P. Eh, eh. Be nice to your abuela.
Buenas. Respect noted. Guantería Antigua, 13 P. That's my number.

¡Buenos días, hijo! Forty years, sí, and still my same wobbly table. You like La Rosaleda? For that one I ask 29. A pretty card, she finishes a page beautifully. Have you eaten yet? Take your time, cariño, no hurry here.

You again. Palacio de Velázquez. Thirty-three P. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.
No. 13 P, and I'm being generous.
